html:
The Anglo-Zanzibar War was fought on the morning of 27 August 1896 between Britain and the sultanate of Zanzibar, and lasted about 40 minutes, the shortest war on record.

When the sultan died, his relative Khalid bin Barghash took the throne without British approval. Britain, which had made Zanzibar a protectorate in 1890, gave him an ultimatum. When it ran out, Royal Navy ships shelled the palace, killing hundreds of his defenders.

Khalid fled to the German consulate, and Britain installed a more pliant sultan. The war showed the reality of British power in Zanzibar, whose sultans had ruled since the move from Oman, built on clove plantations. They kept their throne until the revolution of 1964.
sum: The Anglo-Zanzibar War was fought on the morning of 27 August 1896 between Britain and the sultanate of Zanzibar, and lasted about 40 minutes, the shortest war on record.
